narrative.northStar: The Voice Note, Glowing After Dark
narrative.overview:
Sawti's landing page refuses the two defaults its category ships by reflex: the gamified-mascot language app and the blue corporate-SaaS dashboard with a mic icon bolted onto a hero. Instead, the page IS a voice note — the exact object Arabic-speaking WhatsApp users already send fifty times a day — enlarged until it becomes the whole interface. Two real message bubbles (a tutor's Arabic prompt, a learner's Dutch reply) form a live conversation thread above the fold, leading the eye down to one oversized circular mic button that glows like a lit object against a dark, lamplit ground — the single largest, most saturated thing on the page. CEFR progress (A0→B1) reads as a row of read-receipt-style chips rather than a gamified progress bar — "your voice notes so far," not points.
The scene this palette answers to: a learner practicing quietly in the evening, phone screen lighting a dim room after a full day of work or family duties — not a bright office SaaS demo. A deep, warm espresso-brown ground carries that scene, lit by one vivid coral accent glowing at page-center like the phone's own light. One color is held in total reserve: emerald appears nowhere except the live-recording state, so its appearance always means "this is listening right now."
keyCharacteristics: A dark, warm ("lamplit," not corporate-black) ground makes the coral mic CTA read as a genuinely glowing object, not a flat colored circle.
Chat-bubble vocabulary (waveform, timestamp, read-receipt tick) carries the entire visual system, not just the demo thread.
RTL is structural, not mirrored decoration: Arabic chrome flows right-to-left natively; Dutch phrases are isolated LTR islands (dir="ltr" lang="nl") inside the RTL flow.
Emerald is a state color, not a palette color — it exists only while something is actively being recorded.
No kickers, no icon-tile feature grids, no gamification chrome (badges, streaks, confetti).

rules.name: The Emerald Reservation Rule
rules.body: Emerald never appears at rest. Its only triggers are the live-recording state (.mic-cta.is-recording), the single CEFR level currently in progress, and the keyboard focus ring.

rules.name: The Bright/Deep Split Rule
rules.body: Coral (bright) is for icon-only surfaces, rendered in Ground. Coral Deep is for any surface holding body text, rendered in Paper. Never reverse the pairing — this split exists because the design already failed that exact contrast check once and had to be fixed.

rules.name: The Two-Surface Text Rule
rules.body: Only the learner bubble card uses dark-on-light text (Ink / Ink Soft). Everywhere else on the page is light-on-dark (Paper / Text Soft on Ground, or Paper on a saturated fill).

rules.name: The Glow-Versus-Ground Rule
rules.body: A saturated fill (coral, emerald) gets a hue-matched glow shadow. A light neutral card (the learner bubble) gets a neutral near-black grounding shadow instead.

rules.name: The Isolated Script Rule
rules.body: Any Dutch (Latin-script) content inside the RTL page is wrapped in its own dir="ltr" lang="nl" span so bidi punctuation and word order never scramble.

dos: Do keep Emerald exclusive to the live-recording state, the single in-progress CEFR level, and the focus ring.
Do put icon-only content on bright Coral in Ground, and body text on Coral Deep in Paper — never the reverse.
Do default new text to light-on-dark (Paper/Text Soft on Ground) and reserve dark-on-light (Ink/Ink Soft) for content inside a light card like the learner bubble.
Do give a saturated fill a hue-matched glow shadow and a light neutral card a neutral grounding shadow.
Do wrap any Latin-script (Dutch) text embedded in the RTL flow in dir="ltr" lang="nl".
donts: Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above the headline, a features-grid of icon+heading+text cards, or gamification chrome (streaks, badges, confetti, points).
Don't default to cream-background-plus-calligraphy for "an Arabic app" — that rendering was named and rejected during this build's direction round.
Don't treat this dark mode as cold or corporate — Ground is a warm espresso-brown meant to feel like a lit phone screen in a dim room.

Don't apply opacity-based dimming to text that needs to stay ≥4.5:1 — this caused a real contrast failure during the first, light-mode build; the Bright/Deep Split Rule exists so the dark palette doesn't repeat it.
Don't mirror the layout as if it were LTR-flipped; RTL here is native document flow, so first-DOM-child-at-the-right is correct, unforced behavior.
